studies.headline: Merops apiaster occupies about as much of the region as it did thirty years ago.
studies.value: +0.022 in the probability a cell is occupied
studies.detail: Occupancy 0.620 in 1987-1991 against 0.642 in 2008-2012, over 496 quarter-degree cells atlassed at least 20 times in both epochs. Detection was estimated separately in each epoch at 0.175 and 0.212.
studies.caveat: Two atlases thirty years apart, so this is a before and after and not a trend: nothing here is per decade. South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini only, and only where volunteers atlassed twice. Nothing here says why.

rows.label: Reporting rate, uncorrected
rows.detail: 0.619 to 0.641 — the share of cells the bird was seen in at all, which is what the answer would have been without a detection model

rows.label: Against the other five-year window

studies.headline: Coccopygia melanotis occupies about as much of the region as it did thirty years ago.
studies.value: -0.058 in the probability a cell is occupied
studies.detail: Occupancy 0.396 in 1987-1991 against 0.338 in 2008-2012, over 496 quarter-degree cells atlassed at least 20 times in both epochs. Detection was estimated separately in each epoch at 0.095 and 0.113.
studies.caveat: Two atlases thirty years apart, so this is a before and after and not a trend: nothing here is per decade. South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini only, and only where volunteers atlassed twice. Nothing here says why.
